seo.title: Sphere Volume Calculator - Spherical Tank
seo.description: Calculate sphere volume in liters or m³ from diameter. For spherical storage tanks, LPG vessels, and gas holders.

formula.explanation: V = (4/3)πr³ = πD³/6. ×1000 converts m³ to liters. Spheres are optimal for pressurized storage (minimum wall stress per unit volume).

content.introduction: Calculate volume of a sphere from diameter. Spherical tanks are widely used for LPG, propane, butane, and cryogenic storage because their shape provides uniform stress distribution under pressure, minimizing wall thickness requirements.

example.description: 10m diameter sphere = 523,599 liters (~524 m³) — typical small LPG sphere.

faq.q: Why use spherical tanks for pressurized storage?
faq.a: A sphere has minimum surface area per unit volume and uniform membrane stress distribution, requiring less steel than a cylinder for the same pressure and volume.
Common sizes range from 100 m³ (6m diameter) to 10,000 m³+ (27m diameter) for refinery and petrochemical applications.
